parsed.notes: Lens A review found one materially bad harvested pinpoint and three quote-format fidelity defects; no Lens A treatment finding is raised.

defect.evidence_quote:
enter a home without a warrant if he has “an objectively
reasonable basis for believing that an occupant is seriously
injured or imminently threatened with such injury.”
Brigham City, 547 U. S., at 400. The officers’ entry satisfied
that test.
defect.locator_note: pin-slip10; content_page.md line 59; text slip op. 10-11
defect.problem: The slip-10 quote is supported at slip op. 10-11, but it is not character-faithful: it replaces the opinion's curly quotation marks and apostrophe with straight quotes and uses an ellipsis where the source contains the Brigham City citation.
defect.proposed_fix: Either preserve the source punctuation/citation in the quoted text or convert the passage to a paraphrase.

reasons: The quoted proposition appears in the opinion and the slip-op locator is right.
The lake record itself flags this pinpoint as quote_fidelity=mismatch.
residual_risks: Only quote fidelity was attacked; support otherwise appears sound from the disclosed text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use exact source quotation marks and include or accurately elide the Brigham City citation.

defect.evidence_quote:
But Brigham City did not adopt
Terry’s reasonable-suspicion standard for home entries
defect.locator_note: pin-slip7; content_page.md line 53; text slip op. 7
defect.problem: The pin-slip7 payload is not the opinion passage; it appears to have harvested content-page prose/Markdown beginning with 'doctrine. ## Issue...' rather than the slip-op text.
defect.proposed_fix: Rebuild pin-slip7 from the actual slip-op page 7 passage, preserving source punctuation, or remove the verbatim-quote claim.

reasons: The asserted payload quote contains page headings and prose not found in the opinion text.
The actual slip-op page 7 passage begins with the Brigham City/Terry discussion.
residual_risks: After rebuilding the pin, the replacement quote still needs exact punctuation/ellipsis review.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the bad harvested payload with the actual slip-op passage at text lines 364-372.

defect.evidence_quote:
We decline Case’s invitation to put a new probable-cause
spin onto Brigham City.
defect.locator_note: pin-slip8; content_page.md line 55; text slip op. 8
defect.problem: The slip-8 quote lands on the right passage, but it is not character-faithful because it changes source punctuation, including Case’s apostrophe and quotation marks around the Brigham City phrase.
defect.proposed_fix: Preserve source punctuation in the quoted fragments or mark the sentence as a paraphrase.

reasons: The substance and slip-op page are supported by the opinion.
The displayed quote uses straight punctuation where the disclosed text uses typographic punctuation.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use source-faithful punctuation and retain a clear ellipsis for omitted intervening material.

defect.evidence_quote:
that an emergency-aid entry provides no basis to search the
premises beyond what is reasonably needed to deal with the
emergency while maintaining the officers’ safety.
defect.locator_note: pin-slip9; content_page.md line 57; text slip op. 9
defect.problem: The slip-9 quote is supported, but it is not character-faithful because it omits the lead-in without marking the cut and changes officers’ to officers'.
defect.proposed_fix: Quote the passage with source punctuation and either include the lead-in or mark the sentence-opening omission.

reasons: The scope-limitation language appears at the cited slip page.
The quote is not character-exact against the disclosed text.
residual_risks: No support defect found beyond quote formatting.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use '[a]n emergency-aid entry' or include 'that an emergency-aid entry' and preserve officers’.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no treatment defect is raised.
The treatment payload matches the lake record's disclosed good_law judgment and scope note.
The opinion text confirms the January 14, 2026 decision date and that Kagan wrote for a unanimous Court with Sotomayor and Gorsuch concurring.
residual_risks: Currency beyond the disclosed lake judgment was not independently evaluated under Lens A.
